claims.claim: A sail should be neither over-sheeted nor over-eased.

lines.en: Today we are not hunting: we will come up slowly, under sail alone, behind a whale. Mestre Manuel asks for the sail neither too tight nor too loose.
lines.pt: Hoje não vamos à caça: vamos chegar devagar, só à vela, por trás de uma baleia. O Mestre Manuel pede a vela nem caçada demais, nem folgada demais.

claims.claim: A sail should be neither over-sheeted nor over-eased.

lines.en: Quiet on board, please. We want to get close without noise, with only the wind. Mestre Manuel looks at the sail: "Not too tight, not too loose, lad."
lines.pt: Silêncio a bordo, por favor. Queremos aproximar-nos sem ruído, só com o vento. O Mestre Manuel olha para a vela: "Nem muito caçada, nem muito solta, rapaz."

lines.en: Ease, ease. Slower.
lines.pt: Folga, folga. Mais devagar.

lines.en: Ease the sail, lad.
lines.pt: Folga a vela, rapaz.

lines.en: Now we wait. You do not chase.
lines.pt: Agora esperamos. Não se corre atrás.

lines.en: Leave her be. We stay here, no hurry.
lines.pt: Deixa-a. Ficamos aqui, sem pressa.

lines.en: Bear away a little.
lines.pt: Arriba um pouco.

lines.en: Bear away, bear away. Gently.
lines.pt: Arriba, arriba. Devagar.

claims.claim: The sail flapping is called panejar (luffing).
Luffing comes from over-easing the sheet or pointing closer to the wind than close-hauled.

lines.en: — What was that noise? — Luffing, panejar. You eased too much, or pointed closer to the wind than you should. A noisy sail does not arrive quietly.
lines.pt: — Que barulho era aquele? — Panejar. Folgaste demais, ou foste mais ao vento do que devias. Vela que faz barulho não chega calada.

claims.claim: Luffing comes from over-easing the sheet or pointing closer to the wind than close-hauled.

lines.en: — Why was the sail flapping? — It luffs when you ease too much or point too close to the wind. And that way she hears us coming.
lines.pt: — A vela batia porquê? — Paneja quando se folga demais ou se aponta demasiado ao vento. E assim ela ouve-nos chegar.

claims.claim: A sail eased too much deflects less air.
A sail sheeted too tight breaks the airflow.

lines.en: See? Too loose, it deflects less air. Too tight, it breaks the airflow. Stay in between, lad, and listen to it.
lines.pt: Vês? Folgada demais, desvia menos ar. Caçada demais, quebra o escoamento. Fica no meio, rapaz, e escuta-a.

claims.claim: Luffing is the sail flapping irregularly.

lines.en: — How do I know it is right? — When it does not luff and does not go hard. Look: there it is, still. The boat likes light hands.
lines.pt: — Como sei que está bem? — Quando não paneja e não fica dura. Olha: está ali, quieta. O barco gosta de mãos leves.

claims.claim: With a beam wind, an over-sheeted sail breaks the airflow.

lines.en: With the wind on the beam, a sail sheeted too tight breaks the air. Ease just a touch. Like that. You hear nothing, do you?
lines.pt: Com o vento pelo través, vela muito caçada quebra o ar. Folga só um nada. Assim. Não se ouve nada, pois não?

lines.en: (Silence.) This boat has known other days. Today it only watches. Ease a touch, lad, let it sit.
lines.pt: (Silêncio.) Este barco já conheceu outros dias. Hoje só olha. Folga um nada, rapaz, deixa-o ficar.

claims.claim: A sail should be neither over-sheeted nor over-eased.

lines.en: (Manuel is silent for a good while.) Neither tight nor loose. Let it breathe, and us too.
lines.pt: (Manuel cala-se um bom bocado.) Nem caçada nem solta. Deixa-a respirar, e a nós também.

lines.en: She is gone. We watched her, we did not hunt her, and that is what you take home. Mestre Manuel only says: "Good boat." We head back to Horta.
lines.pt: Ela foi-se. Vimo-la, não a caçámos, e é isso que levam para casa. O Mestre Manuel só diz: "Bom barco." Voltamos para a Horta.

lines.en: Today we watched, we did not hunt. Thank you for the quiet. Mestre Manuel runs a hand along the gunwale: "She behaved well." Course for Horta.
lines.pt: Hoje observámos, não caçámos. Obrigado pelo silêncio. O Mestre Manuel passa a mão pela borda: "Portou-se bem." Rumo à Horta.

claims.claim: A sail should be neither over-sheeted nor over-eased.
Panejar is the sail flapping from over-easing or pointing closer to the wind than close-hauled.

lines.en: What is real? The guide, Mestre Manuel and the young crew member are invented. The sailing terms used on board come from sources: a sail should be neither too tight nor too loose, and "panejar" is the sail flapping when it is eased too much or pointed too close to the wind.
lines.pt: O que é real? O guia, o Mestre Manuel e o jovem tripulante são inventados. Os termos de vela usados a bordo vêm de fontes: a vela não deve estar caçada nem folgada demais, e "panejar" é a vela a bater quando se folga demais ou se aponta demasiado ao vento.

claims.claim: Too loose deflects less air; too tight breaks the airflow.
Luffing comes from over-easing the sheet or pointing closer to the wind than close-hauled.

lines.en: On this trip, the people are fiction. The sail is not: too loose deflects less air, too tight breaks the airflow. And when it luffs, it was eased too much or pointed too close to the wind.
lines.pt: Nesta viagem, as pessoas são de ficção. A vela não: demasiado folgada desvia menos ar, demasiado caçada quebra o escoamento. E quando paneja, folgou-se demais ou foi-se demasiado ao vento.

lines.en: Very well!
lines.pt: Muito bem!

lines.en: That's it.
lines.pt: Isso mesmo.

lines.en: Good, that's right.
lines.pt: Boa, assim está bem.

lines.en: Perfect, keep going.
lines.pt: Perfeito, continue.

lines.en: Like that.
lines.pt: Assim.

lines.en: That's it, lad.
lines.pt: Isso, rapaz.

lines.en: Good.
lines.pt: Bom.

lines.en: All right. Easy.
lines.pt: Está bem. Devagar.

lines.en: Nice!
lines.pt: Boa!

lines.en: Wow, just like that.
lines.pt: Uau, assim mesmo.

lines.en: It worked!
lines.pt: Funcionou!

lines.en: Looks right, doesn't it?
lines.pt: Ficou bem, não ficou?

claims.claim: Caravels were lateen-rigged vessels adapted and improved for difficult long-distance Discovery voyages.

lines.en: Caravels, lateen-rigged, were adapted and improved for the long, difficult voyages of the Discoveries.
lines.pt: As caravelas, de vela latina, foram adaptadas e melhoradas para as longas e difíceis viagens dos Descobrimentos.
lines.speaker: k1

claims.claim: In Lisbon, fishing 'do alto' meant fishing beyond the river bar, not at a set distance from the coast.
The bar is the entrance of the Tagus at Lisbon.

lines.en: In Lisbon, fishing 'do alto' meant fishing beyond the Tagus bar, not at a set distance from the coast.
lines.pt: Em Lisboa, pescar «do alto» queria dizer pescar para lá da barra do Tejo, e não a uma distância certa da costa.
lines.speaker: k1

claims.claim: Caravels from Galicia sailed to Cabo Branco to fish sharks and mullets.
The fish were dried in the sun like cod from Newfoundland.

lines.en: Caravels from Galicia sailed to Cabo Branco to fish sharks and mullets, dried in the sun like Newfoundland cod.
lines.pt: Caravelas da Galiza iam a Cabo Branco pescar tubarões e tainhas, que secavam ao sol, como o bacalhau da Terra Nova.
lines.speaker: k1

claims.claim: A sail should be neither over-sheeted nor over-eased.
Too loose deflects less air; too tight breaks the airflow.

lines.en: Not too tight, not too loose, lad. Too loose, the sail turns little air; too tight, it breaks the flow.
lines.pt: Nem caçada de mais, nem folgada de mais, rapaz. Folgada, a vela desvia pouco ar; caçada de mais, quebra o vento nela.
lines.speaker: k2

claims.claim: Smoked or salted fish was shipped to Castile, Aragon, Italy, England and Flanders.

lines.en: Smoked or salted fish went to Castile, Aragon, Italy, England and Flanders, lad.
lines.pt: O peixe fumado ou salgado seguia para Castela, Aragão, Itália, Inglaterra e Flandres, rapaz.
lines.speaker: k2

claims.claim: Pilots worked at the bar of the Tagus at Lisbon.
Fishing outside the bar was authorised.

lines.en: I heard pilots worked at the Tagus bar, and that fishing outside it was allowed.
lines.pt: Ouvi dizer que na barra do Tejo trabalhavam pilotos, e que lá fora era permitido pescar.
lines.speaker: k3

claims.claim: Coastal navigation included trips to the Algarve to fetch produce.
Coastal navigation included trade with Moroccan ports.

lines.en: In coastal navigation, boats went to the Algarve to fetch produce, or to trade with Moroccan ports.
lines.pt: Na navegação costeira, os barcos iam ao Algarve buscar produtos, ou comerciar com portos de Marrocos.
lines.speaker: k1

claims.claim: Fish preserved by salting and curing was kept in fishermen's houses.
Salted and cured fish was sold alongside fresh fish.

lines.en: Salted and cured fish was kept in fishermen's houses, and sold alongside fresh fish.
lines.pt: O peixe salgado e curado ficava em casa dos pescadores, e vendia-se ao lado do peixe fresco.
lines.speaker: k3
